SUMMARY

Bristol-Myers Squibb Company(BMY+0.67%)reported a 7% increase in total revenue for the third quarter, supported by 12% expansion in its growth portfolio medicines. Management raised the full-year revenue outlook and emphasized progress in transitioning its oncology franchise to subcutaneous formulations like Qvantig. The company continues to invest in its late-stage pipeline with recent positive readouts in radiopharmaceuticals and cell therapies while managing upcoming loss of exclusivity impacts for its cardiovascular franchise in international markets.

Operator:Welcome to the Bristol Myers Squibb Third Quarter 26 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in a listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask a question, you may press *1. On your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, please press *2. Please note this event is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Charles E. Triano, Senior Vice President and Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Charles E. Triano:Thank you, and good morning, everyone. We appreciate you joining our third quarter 2 thousand 26 earnings call. With me this morning with prepared remarks are Christopher S. Boerner, our Board Chair and Chief executive officer, and David V. Elkins, our chief financial officer. Also participating in today's call is Adam Lenkowsky, our Chief Commercialization and Cristian Massacesi, our chief medical officer and head of global drug development. Earlier this morning, we posted our quarterly slide presentation to bms.com, that you can use to follow along with Christopher and David's remarks. Before we get started, I will remind everybody that during this call, we will make statements about the company's future plans and prospects that constitute forward looking statements.

Actual results may differ materially from those indicated by those forward looking statements as a result of various important factors, including those discussed in the company's SEC filings. These forward looking statements represent our estimates as of today and should not be relied upon as representing our estimates as of any future date. And we specifically disclaim any obligation to update forward looking statements even if our estimates change. We will also focus our comments on our non GAAP financial measures, which are adjusted to exclude certain specified items. Reconciliations of certain non GAAP financial measures to the most comparable GAAP measure are available at bms.com.

Finally, unless otherwise stated, all comparisons are made from the same period in 2025 and sales growth rates will be discussed on an underlying basis which excludes the impact of foreign exchange. All references to our P and L are on a non GAAP basis. And with that, I will hand it over to Christopher.

Christopher S. Boerner:Thanks, Chuck. Morning, everyone, and thank you for joining our Q3 2026 earnings call. We reported another quarter of double digit growth in our growth portfolio and progressed our plans to derisk the pipeline to position the company for long term success. We have seen several positive registrational readouts and regulatory approvals over the past few months and we expect more to come. Bringing the next wave of launches into sharper focus. We are executing well commercially Our differentiated pipeline is advancing nicely. And we continue to operate with discipline which gives us strategic flexibility to invest for sustainable growth.

Based on the strength of our results, we are raising our full year guidance David will provide additional details on this shortly. Let me start with our Q3 performance on Slide 4. Our growth portfolio continues to deliver solid results with sales increasing 12%. Driven by a broad set of differentiated products. We generated strong performance in key brands including Reblozyl, Breonzi, Optulag, Qvantig and Camzyos. We also continue to expand the reach of our medicines. In September, Camzyos received approval for an expanded indication and became the only FDA approved therapy for pediatric patients with obstructive HCM. We also achieved an important milestone in the quarter with the FDA's accelerated approval of Symvexis.

The first approved CELMoD, and the newest addition to our portfolio. Symvexis is approved for the treatment of multiple myeloma where combination of a highly efficacious and convenient oral option is an important treatment advancement for patients in both community and academic settings. We are encouraged by positive early launch feedback and by the compelling Phase 3 data we announced earlier this month whereas Symvexis' demonstrated a meaningful improvement in progression free survival. We will present these data at ASH in December. These results further strengthen our conviction in CELMoDs and our broader targeted protein degradation platform, where BMS is a clear leader. Behind Symvexis, our second cell mod, Mezigdomide, has a PDUFA date of 05/13/2027.

Mezigdomide offers the potential to introduce another highly efficacious and convenient oral option for a different segment of multiple myeloma patients. We also continue to advance glaucamide in lymphoma and will present the first phase 2 data in frontline follicular lymphoma at ASH. The momentum in our late stage pipeline has accelerated. In the past 2 months alone, we announced positive data for 4 registrational studies. These include Symvexis PFS, as I mentioned earlier, admilparant in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, interim results for RAISE 101 in GEP-NETs, and Arlocell in relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma. Let me comment on the last 3.

Admilpirant met its primary endpoint at the 60 milligram dose with a favorable safety and tolerability profile that supports its potential as a first in class IPF treatment. IPF is a progressive and often fatal disease where there remains a need for effective, well tolerated treatment options like admilparant. We will discuss the IPF results with regulators and expect phase 3 results in progressive pulmonary fibrosis in the first quarter of next year. Is a larger opportunity in another area admilparant has significant commercial potential. With respect to RAISE 101, our actinium based radiopharmaceutical therapy, we are encouraged by the interim readouts in GEP-NETs.

These results demonstrated a clinically meaningful improvement in PFS in patients whose disease has progressed following existing lutetium based therapy. These were the first phase 3 results for an alpha emitting targeted RPT. Representing an important milestone for RAISE 101 and further strengthening our conviction in radiopharmaceuticals as a platform. We are engaging with the FDA on next steps towards regulatory submission. Finally, Arlocelll, our GPRC5D directed CAR T, delivered positive results in the registrational phase 2 quintessential study this September. A milestone that underscores its potential to set a new standard of care in the post BCMA multiple myeloma market.

This study represents the only prospective trial exclusively conducted in the post BCMA quadruple class exposed setting a growing patient population with poor outcomes and no therapies approved specifically for this segment. As these programs advance, we are building the manufacturing foundation for the next generation of our medicines with 2 US investments recently announced. In Houston, we shared plans for a new state of the art campus at Generation Park an approximately $2.3 billion investment that will create nearly 500 skilled jobs. This facility, will give us manufacturing flexibility across small molecules, biologics, and antibody drug conjugates. It is also designed to evolve and scale to meet patient needs for decades to come.

In Indiana, RYZ is investing more than $170 million to establish a new radiopharmaceutical manufacturing facility complementing its existing footprint in the state and creating up to 100 new jobs by the end of 29. Together, these investments support the next wave of medicines coming through our pipeline and advance our US manufacturing commitments. Turning to slide 5. As we look ahead, we have several meaningful readouts over the remainder of 2026 and into 2027. Before year end, we expect Phase 3 data for Milvexian in secondary stroke prevention and Sotyktu in lupus. With that, we will share open label Alzheimer's disease psychosis data from the ADEPT-1 and from the long term extension ADEPT-3 studies at CTAD next month.

In 2027, we continue to expect results for Milvexian in atrial fibrillation in the first quarter, We also anticipate additional data from the broader ADEPT program, bipolar I data from the BALSAM-1 studies, and the first registrational data for glaukatamide in high risk first line LBCL. So while we have made good progress in our pipeline, there is more to come. As we close out the year and move into 2027, we are focused on a few key priorities as noted on slide 6. First, sustaining the momentum across our growth portfolio. We now have 8 growth portfolio medicines, each annualizing over $1 billion based on Q3 sales, giving us a broad base of growth drivers.

Second, translating pipeline progress into filings, approvals and successful launches. ZYNBEXIS is an early example of that progression, and as additional studies read out, our focus will be on launch preparedness and moving with urgency to bring these medicines to patients. Third, continuing to rewire how we operate. We are focused on becoming faster and more efficient in R&D, And over the past year, we have made changes across the organization to strengthen how we design and conduct clinical trials. At the same time, continue to drive productivity and efficiency including through our organizational structure, capital allocation decision making process, and the use of technology.

That discipline gives us flexibility to invest behind the growth portfolio and pipeline pursue business development where it makes sense, and return cash to shareholders. Taken together, we are entering the final quarter of the year with real momentum. Our growth portfolio is performing well, We are advancing our pipeline with meaningful wins and remain highly disciplined in ensuring our cost structure is aligned with our revenue base. The team is energized focused on delivering value for patients and our shareholders. With that, I will turn it over to David.

David V. Elkins:Thank you, Christopher S. Boerner, and good morning, everyone. Our third quarter results reflect continued strong execution of our growth portfolio and continued strength from Eliquis. We remain focused on financial discipline, balancing investments in our growth drivers with continued productivity improvements. Based on our performance year to date and our outlook for the remainder of the year, we are further raising our full year guidance. Let me begin with a review of our third quarter results. Starting with slide 8, total revenue in the third quarter increased 7% year over year to $13.1 billion Growth portfolio revenue rose 12% to $7.7 billion driven by double digit growth across several products.

Our legacy portfolio revenue increased 1% with growth in Eliquis more than offsetting the declines from generic entry across the remainder of the legacy portfolio. Turning to product performance on slide 9, starting with oncology. For Opdivo, revenue decreased 6% year over year to $2.4 billion primarily reflecting continued conversion to Qvantig in The U. S. And in Europe. Qvantig continued its strong launch trajectory with revenue of $334 million representing sequential growth of 28%. And is now annualizing at over $1.3 billion. Opdualag delivered another quarter of strong double digit growth driven by continued global demand and its leading position as a standard of care in first line melanoma in The U. S. Turning to slide 10.

Reblozyl grew 22% to $750 million reflecting continued strength in first-line MDS associated anemia. Breyanzi posted 48% growth resulting in revenue of $526 million driven by its best in class profile and strong demand in both the U.S. and in international markets. Moving to cardiovascular and immunology on slide 11. Eliquis revenue was $4.7 billion up 26% driven by net price along with strong demand and continued market share gains. Eliquis sales in Q4 will be impacted by the upcoming LOE in Europe, which will be partially offset by the continued growth in the U.S. Camzyos' revenue increased 42% to $420 million reflecting continued strong demand growth, including new patient starts, and deeper penetration into the community setting.

On a sequential basis revenue was impacted by the typical inventory drawdown during the third quarter. Which we expect will normalize in the fourth quarter. Now moving to immunology. Global revenue for Sotyktu grew 25%, We are supporting the recent indication for psoriatic arthritis in adults. And look forward to the upcoming phase 3 readouts in lupus expected by year end. I will wrap up our product performance review on slide 12. With neuroscience, the Cobenfy revenue grew 33% to $57 million in the quarter. On a sequential basis, inventory destocking offset increased demand. We anticipate that revenue will more closely track prescription volume going forward. Let's now move to the P and L on Slide 13.

Gross margin in the third quarter was 68.4% reflecting product mix and to a lesser extent a 1 time expense for a contract termination. Operating expenses for the third quarter were $4.1 billion. We continue to benefit from our strategic productivity initiative which is enabling us to reduce expenses in identified areas while maintaining flexibility to invest in multiple growth oriented opportunities. Our effective tax rate in the quarter was 14.1%, reflecting jurisdictional earnings mix and the impact of an acquired in process R&D charge. And we had a $0.58 per share impact from acquired in process R&D and licensing income in the quarter. Considering all these factors, diluted earnings per share was $1.35 for the quarter.

Turning to the balance sheet and capital allocation highlights on Slide 14. We remain in a solid financial position, with approximately $13 billion in cash equivalents and marketable securities as of September 30. And we generated approximately $4.2 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter. In terms of capital allocation, maintain a strategic and balanced approach to deploying our strong cash flows. Business development remains a priority. And we are regularly evaluating opportunities in the therapeutic areas we know best while continuing to return cash to our shareholders through our commitment to the dividend. Now moving to guidance on Slide 15.

We are increasing our full year revenue guidance based upon our year to date results and our current projections for the balance of the year. Excluding the third quarter acquired in process R&D charges and licensing income of $0.58 per share, the midpoint of our 2026 non GAAP EPS guidance would have increased by approximately $0.15 per share. After including the $0.58 per share previously referenced, our expected non GAAP EPS guidance range for 2026 is now $6.35 to $6.55 We are maintaining our projections for gross margin, operating expenses, and tax rate while slightly lowering the expense level on our other income and expense line.

Incorporated into these revisions is a total legacy portfolio revenue decrease now expected to be between 3% to 5%, while we continue to expect Eliquis full year revenue growth of 20% to 25%. In closing, our strong performance year to date reinforces our confidence in the business. We remain focused on executing across our growth portfolio and pipeline, while maintaining financial discipline to deliver long term value for our patients and shareholders. And with that, I will now turn the call back over to Chuck for Q&A.

Instance, the number of discontinuation for adverse event were lower or the same level of placebo. 1 120 milligram going to your question, we have seen an improvement, a decline in FVC but not statistically significant. So we continue to analyze the data. We continue to dig into the data. We will present the data in medical meeting next year. Anyway, we are pleased with this outcome.

Alexandria Hammond:Thanks for taking the question. Thank you.

Charles E. Triano:Thanks for the question, Alexandria.

Adam Lenkowsky:So, Alexandria, we are excited to have launched Symvexis. it is the first approved CELMoD in the market. Now it is still early in the launch, but our teams are executing well. We are pleased with the adoption that we are seeing over the first few weeks on the market, and physician feedback has been positive. Largely based on the strength of the MRD results as well as the simplicity of use. We are seeing use to come from both the community and the hospital setting. Do expect the majority of use to come from the community where 70% to 80% of patients are treated. We will see that longer term.

Our teams are focused on establishing a broad base of prescribers and reinforcing the efficacy, the safety, and quite frankly, the simplicity of using Symvexis replace Revlimid and Pomalyst based regimens. We also are excited about the PFS data, which will further augment the profile and we look forward to presenting these data at ASH. So we are seeing good commercial potential for Symvexis. And for Mezigdomide. We are excited to launch it as well and aim for both products to be foundational therapies in the community by replacing image over time.

Christopher S. Boerner:Thanks, Adam.

Charles E. Triano:Let's take our next question.

Operator:The next question comes from Seamus Fernandez with Guggenheim. Please go ahead.

Seamus Fernandez:Thank you for the question. This is Zach Dunn. On for Seamus Fernandez. To start, as you mentioned, there is been a series of positive Phase III programs that have read out successfully and I am not sure these are getting fully appreciated. So what do you think the market is missing from these readouts? Thank you.

Christopher S. Boerner:Thanks for the question, Ben. Maybe on the Milvexian question, you could start, and then I will close out with just your comments on the market.

Cristian Massacesi:Seamus, started with the readouts. Let me let me go there first. We are pleased. I am pleased to see that this 2026 we are getting a very good pace, a very good flow. Last year, when we started and we discussed, we explained how much scrutiny we put in every trial. To try to mitigate risks that intrinsically every trial may have. And I think it is start to pay off. And what I am pleased that we have a positive outcomes across therapeutic areas. In hematology, in immunology, in we will have cell therapy. So this is, this looks good.

And if we close this year, because there are 3 remaining this year, SSP and the 2 SOTICTO studies in lupus, with positive outcome, I think we can be very pleased on the rate of success that we will score in 2026. Your specific question, SSP, I think I would put in the big picture first. This study was designed based on a very solid phase 2 trial. That we run showing 30 percent risk reduction in strokes. and with a very careful selection of the dose, and the benefit risk profile, efficacy, safety. I imagine you refer to the randomization window that may be different compared to some competitive studies.

We based all the criteria when the patients are randomized based on our own Phase II and based on prior Phase III studies. And what I can tell you that the data pointing that the randomization window that we selected can provide, could provide the best efficacy. So we are looking forward to see the SSP data this year. And of course, we are also very eager to see the AFib readout Q1 next year.

Christopher S. Boerner:Ben, the only thing I would just add on top of what Christian just said is in our discussions with investors, we have been very focused on emphasizing that the long term growth that we. The long term focus that we have is building a strong company that can deliver sustained growth, particularly as we get into the next decade. To do that, we think we have got to continue to do, frankly, what we have demonstrated this year, which is drive the business that exists today. You see that in our quarterly postings. Deliver on our late stage pipeline. Christian and team have done a really nice job of scrutinizing those studies.

We are obviously happy with the results that we have seen with Arlocellles and admilparant, and RAISE 101. We are looking forward to the additional readouts we have the rest of this year and into next year. And as we discussed in our prepared remarks, being very disciplined in how we operate, from a financial standpoint and consistently. We are obviously happy with the performance we have seen thus far, but the team is heads down and making sure we continue to deliver across each of those areas, going forward.

Charles E. Triano:Thanks, Christopher.

Christopher S. Boerner:Betsy, let's move to the next question please.

Operator:The next question comes from Akash Tewari with Jeff. Please go ahead.

Akash Tewari:Hey, thanks so much. Can you frame the admilparant opportunity relative to some of the products in the space? And also maybe investor expectations around Milvexian. We are seeing Ofev have 1 of the best launches in IPF despite a modest FTC. And could be a bigger opportunity than IPF. So could this actually be 1 of your biggest products now that you have the IPF data And did admilparant show a benefit on time to event or mortality in your IPF trial? Thank you.

Christopher S. Boerner:Adam, do you want to take that? And then, Cristian, you could chime in.

Adam Lenkowsky:Yeah, Akash, thanks for the question. So you know, we think there is significant need that remains for new and improved disease modifying therapies. Both IPF and that are both effective and well tolerated. And that includes impacting how patients feel, it includes how patients function, and ultimately the impact on survival rates. As you know, it is a dismal survival rate in both IPF and PPF that are we hear from KOLs that taking a holistic approach to the data is going to be important. And that includes, as you mentioned, looking at both the primary and the secondary endpoints of the study. We know that safety and tolerability will be a key area of differentiation for admilparant.

You know, even with the advent of newer therapies, GI tolerability and cough, they are challenging to manage, especially in an older comorbid patient population. And Christian talked about, you know, the aloft study showed a positive impact on FVC but also admilparant demonstrated a well tolerated safety profile where discontinuations due to adverse events were similar to placebo. So there is a real opportunity to gain share as effective and well tolerated treatments like admilparant come to market. Also expect the market to grow significantly. I have talked about this previously where today it is a $4 billion market. We think this market could nearly double.

We are going to start to see the creation of a large second line switch and/or add on market with newer treatments available. We have got a number of prelaunch activities underway. With a focus on bringing in pulmonology expertise to the company providing education to physicians on this new and promising mechanism. And we are also looking forward to the readout early next year because that is the larger commercial opportunity that can complement the IPF results.

Christopher S. Boerner:Thanks, Adam. Anything to add, Cristian?

Operator:Akash, your question is more related to key secondary endpoints, some key secondary endpoints outcomes.

Cristian Massacesi:Did not disclose this. We mentioned we talked in the press release about the primary and some of the safety profile. I can tell you that we are pleased the overall outcome of the trial, and we will present this data in a medical meeting next year.

Christopher S. Boerner:Thanks, Christian.

Charles E. Triano:Let's move to our next question, please.

Matt Phipps:Hi. This is Eric on for Matt Phipps. Just a question on the ADEPT trials. So with ADEPT timelines reiterated for 2027 again, was wondering if you could give some specifics on current enrollment progress as well as site quality remediation and if we should expect the ADEPT 1, 2, and 4 readouts to land together or be more staggered throughout the year?

Charles E. Triano:Thanks for the question. Cristian, do you want to take that?

Cristian Massacesi:Thank you, Matt, for the question. Let me start, actually with the program status as you were asking for. Everything is tracking as we guided. We have a potential interim analysis for ADEPT-1 later this year. And we anticipate the top line results readouts for all the ADEPT program throughout 2027. Some readouts can coincide or can be more or less the same time. Or can be staggered as, you know, ADEPT-1 is event driven, for instance. We. I think Christopher mentioned in his opening remarks that we also expect, on top of that program, the readouts of our bipolar I program in 2027. So very important year for Cobenfy in terms of data flow.

I want to point out 1 aspect that is important to your attention. In November, we look forward to the CTAD presentation in Boston. There, we will present 2 data sets. The first is the open-label lead-in period from the ongoing ADEPT-1 study. And the second data set is from the open label extension, rollover study ADEPT-3. So both course substantial number of patients, all patients treated with Cobenfy. This presentation will address some improvements in psychotic symptoms with KarXT. And of course, we are waiting the randomized control studies, to read out. But I think the CTA data are encouraging in our view. And support I believe is supporting ongoing development programs.

Christopher S. Boerner:Thanks, Cristian. Greg.

Charles E. Triano:Let's move to our next question, please.

Operator:The next question comes from Carter Gould with Carter. Please go ahead.

Carter Gould:Good morning. Thanks for taking the question. You have got a number of small cell lung cancer studies expected to read out over 27 and 28. I was hoping you could talk about your confidence and the relevance of these studies in light of the Bayer frontline data and if that augurs any sort of changes to your strategy. Thank you.

Cristian Massacesi:Cristian? Thank you. Thank you for the good question. The data we have seen at ESMO are quite impressive. And actually, we welcome this data in such a difficult disease, like extended disease and small cell lung cancer. As you said, we have ongoing registrational studies with Biogen's ASO and combination of nivolumab and standard chemotherapy. The study is completed. We are just, now looking at the readout. And we are running the combination with Pumitamig plus standard chemotherapy. We do not know, of course, the outcome of this study and how that can benchmark.

But, I think, these are studies that allow us first of all, to benchmark the activity of a novel mechanism of action like Biogen's ASO, in this space. But targeting an important antigen expressed in most of the patients with tumors, with small cell lung cancer tumors. But also for our PD-1 VEGF, this will give us a benchmark because then we will prepare the next step. As you know, we started the combination with Pumitamig plus the DLL3 T-cell engager from BioNTech that we announced. So we are paving the road with an extra way because we believe our assets can play in this space, of course, through combinations with engagers.

Christopher S. Boerner:I think the only thing I would add is just that as you look at impressive data, and I would agree these are impressive data, over time in all of these hard to treat diseases, small cell being 1 of them, what is likely to occur is you are going to see patients continue to be subtype. And additional therapies be required to treat patients not only in initial lines of therapy, but subsequent lines of therapy and I think at the end of the day, there is gonna be room for multiple agents to, be engaged to help treat these patients.

Charles E. Triano:Thanks, Christopher S. Boerner. Let's take our next question, please.
